questions.stem: Reflect the point (3, 4) across the x-axis. What are the coordinates of the reflected point?
questions.solution: When reflecting a point across the x-axis, only the y-coordinate changes its sign. So, the reflected coordinates are (3, -4).
questions.explanation: Reflecting across the x-axis means keeping the x-coordinate unchanged and changing the sign of the y-coordinate.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to forget to change the sign of the y-coordinate.

questions.stem: Reflect the line segment connecting points (1, 2) and (5, 6) across the x-axis. What are the coordinates of the endpoints of the reflected line segment?
questions.solution: Reflecting a line segment across the x-axis means reflecting each point on the segment. The endpoints become (1, -2) and (5, -6).
questions.explanation: Each point on the original line segment is reflected by changing only the sign of the y-coordinate.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to forget that both endpoints must be reflected.

questions.stem: Reflect the triangle with vertices (2, 1), (4, 3), and (6, 5) across the x-axis. What are the coordinates of the reflected vertex (6, 5)?
questions.solution: Reflecting a vertex across the x-axis means changing only the sign of its y-coordinate. The reflected point is (6, -5).
questions.explanation: The x-coordinate remains unchanged while the y-coordinate changes sign.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to mix up the x- and y-coordinates.

questions.stem: Reflect the parabola defined by the equation y = x^2 across the x-axis. What is the equation of the reflected parabola?
questions.solution: Reflecting a parabola across the x-axis changes the sign of the y-value. The new equation is y = -x^2.
questions.explanation: The reflection affects only the function part of the equation, not the independent variable x.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to forget that the entire function changes sign.

questions.stem: Reflect the circle with center (3, 4) and radius 2 across the x-axis. What are the coordinates of the center of the reflected circle?
questions.solution: Reflecting a circle across the x-axis changes only the sign of its y-coordinate. The center becomes (3, -4).
questions.explanation: The reflection affects only the center coordinates, not the radius.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to forget that only the center's y-coordinate changes.

questions.stem: Reflect the rectangle with vertices (1, 2), (3, 2), (3, 4), and (1, 4) across the x-axis. Which of the following best describes the relationship between the original and reflected rectangles?

choices.B: They are similar but not congruent.
choices.D: They are neither similar nor congruent.

questions.solution: Reflecting a rectangle across the x-axis produces a new rectangle that is congruent to the original one, as it maintains the same shape and size with flipped orientation.
questions.explanation: Reflection preserves shape and size but may change orientation.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to think that reflection changes the size or shape of the figure.

questions.stem: Reflect the function f(x) = 2x + 3 across the x-axis. What is the equation of the reflected function?
questions.solution: Reflecting a linear function across the x-axis changes the sign of the coefficient and constant term. The new equation is f(x) = -2x - 3.
questions.explanation: Reflection affects both the slope and the y-intercept of the line.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to forget that both the slope and the y-intercept change sign.
